draft.title: Secularisation
card: Secularisation is the decline of religion's influence on public life. Public life includes law, government, schools and everyday social habits.
It can show up in fewer people attending religious services or saying they follow a religion. It can also show up in laws and public institutions that are not based on one religion.
Secularisation is uneven. It is stronger in some countries than in others, and stronger among some groups than others, such as different age groups.
Less religious influence in public life does not always mean people have no beliefs. Many people still hold personal beliefs or take part in religious traditions.
draft.remember: Secularisation means religion has less influence on public life, and it happens to different degrees in different places and groups.

a.q: Which example best shows secularisation in a society?
opts: Religious groups have less say over public laws and schools
A religion opens a new place of worship in a suburb
A government bans all beliefs that differ from its own
People of one faith move to a new country together
a.why: Secularisation is a decline in religion's influence on public life, and less say over laws and schools is an example. A new place of worship does not show a decline in that influence, so it is not an example.
a.clue: Look for a drop in religion's influence on public life.

b.q: A survey finds that fewer young people in Country X attend religious services, but older people in Country X still attend in large numbers. What does this best show about secularisation?
opts: It is uneven, as it differs between groups in a society
It is complete, as young people will lead all of society
It has not happened, as older people still attend services
It is the same everywhere, as attendance falls in all groups
b.why: Attendance falls among the young but not among the old, so secularisation varies between groups. It has not simply happened or failed to happen, because the change is partial and differs between groups.
b.clue: Compare the two age groups in the same country.

a.best: Religious groups have less say over public laws and schools

b.best: It is uneven, as it differs between groups in a society
